final_answer:
>>> Imagine a small town where the mayor notices that every time the local ice cream shop sells more ice cream, the number of bicycle accidents in the town also goes up. The mayor starts to worry that ice cream is causing people to have accidents.  

>>> However, a clever resident points out that the real reason might be the weather: on hot days, more people buy ice cream to cool off, and more people also ride their bikes to escape the heat. The heat is the hidden factor—called a "confounding variable"—that causes both ice cream sales and bike accidents to rise.  

>>> This thought experiment shows that just because two things happen together (correlation), it doesn’t mean one causes the other (causation). The real cause could be something else entirely!
